correctness.rationale: For each degree-two prescribed target, semisimple coefficients of a square root vanish, leaving exactly n free degree-two coefficients and a cyclic system u_i u_{i+1}=c_i. The weighted-independent-set and gap formulas cover zero, mixed, and full supports with consistent endpoints and q-1 propagations. A four-state transfer trace counts admissible target supports, and the toric correction covers parity and square-class effects. The nonnegative matrix is primitive with eigenvalue strictly between q-1 and q, proving sharp exponential density. The embedded standard-library checker exhaustively verifies every target for fourteen prime/prime-power configurations, including F4; such finite testing is not taken as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The two genuinely assessed claims are the prescribed singular (mixed-zero/nonzero) target fibers in a cyclic Loewy-three radical, and the all-target square-image transfer law with exponential rate. The full-support multiplicative consistency rule is known toric mathematics and is expressly not novel. The inspected material did not imply the singular-support law. A possibility of earlier graph monomial-map generality remains documented.

value.rationale: Squaring is a canonical polynomial map on the Jacobson radical of a finite-dimensional algebra. The mixed-zero singular strata exhibit a sharp obstructor (a single zero edge between nonzero edges), exact multiplicities indexed by intrinsic cyclic gap lengths, and a complete field-uniform image-density law with a strict Perron entropy constant. These structurally classify an infinite natural family, instead of rephrasing a small table or toric special case.
